name: indefinite integral (measure with a density)
description: For a measure mu and nonnegative measurable f, the measure nu(A)=int_A f dmu, written nu=f.mu, which is absolutely continuous with respect to mu with Radon-Nikodym derivative f.

name: kernel-built product measure (mu (x) K)
description: The measure on the product space X x Y defined by (mu (x) K)(A x B)=int_A K(x,B)mu(dx), uniquely extending Fubini-type integration int f d(mu (x) K)=int mu(dx) int K(x,dy)f(x,y) when the second coordinate is governed by a transition kernel.

name: moments, variance, and covariance
description: The n-th moment E[X^n], the variance Var(X)=E[(X-EX)^2], and the covariance Cov(X,Y)=E[(X-EX)(Y-EY)] of integrable random variables, the basic numerical summaries of a distribution's spread and dependence.

name: law of the unconscious statistician (expectation via distribution)
description: Computes E[g(X)] as the integral int g(x) mu_X(dx) against the law of X rather than against the underlying probability measure, transferring expectation computations to the distribution.

name: Doob-Dynkin lemma
description: A random variable Y is sigma(X)-measurable if and only if Y=g(X) for some Borel-measurable function g, characterizing sigma(X)-measurability as functional dependence on X.

name: de la Vallee-Poussin criterion for uniform integrability
description: A family is uniformly integrable if and only if there exists an increasing convex function phi with phi(t)/t->infinity such that sup_n E[phi(|X_n|)]<infinity, giving a verifiable moment-growth test for uniform integrability.

name: conditional independence given a sigma-algebra
description: Sub-sigma-algebras F and H are conditionally independent given G if E[FH|G]=E[F|G]E[H|G] for bounded F- and H-measurable F,H, i.e. they are independent under the conditional measure given G.

name: substitution (freezing) rule for conditional expectation
description: If X is G-measurable and Y is independent of G, then E[g(X,Y)|G]=h(X) where h(x)=E[g(x,Y)], allowing the G-measurable argument to be frozen as a constant and the independent argument integrated out.

name: Gaussian random vector
description: A random vector X in R^n such that every linear combination <a,X> is a one-dimensional Gaussian, equivalently with characteristic function exp(i<a,mu>-1/2 a^T Sigma a) determined by mean mu and covariance Sigma.

name: Gaussian process
description: A stochastic process (X_t) all of whose finite-dimensional distributions are multivariate Gaussian, completely specified by its mean function m(t)=E[X_t] and covariance kernel C(s,t)=Cov(X_s,X_t).

name: progressively measurable process
description: A process X such that for each t the map (s,omega)->X_s(omega) restricted to [0,t] x Omega is B([0,t]) (x) F_t-measurable; a measurability strengthening of adaptedness ensuring stopped values are measurable.

name: Doob decomposition (discrete time)
description: Every integrable adapted discrete-time process decomposes uniquely as X_n=X_0+M_n+A_n with M a martingale and A a predictable process started at 0; A is increasing iff X is a submartingale.

name: square-integrable martingale
description: A cadlag martingale M with sup_t E[M_t^2]<infinity (or E[M_t^2]<infinity for all t), the natural class on which the L^2 theory of stochastic integration and the bracket <M> is built.

name: optional quadratic variation [M]
description: The adapted increasing process [M]_t=lim sum (M_{t_{i+1}}-M_{t_i})^2 along refining partitions, equal to the continuous part <M^c> plus the sum of squared jumps sum_{s<=t}(Delta M_s)^2, making M^2-[M] a local martingale.

name: quadratic covariation [M,N]
description: The finite-variation process [M,N]=1/4([M+N]-[M-N]) obtained by polarization, satisfying MN-[M,N] is a local martingale and giving the cross term in the integration-by-parts formula for semimartingales.

name: Ito isometry for martingale integrands
description: Establishes E[(int H dM)_t^2]=E[int_0^t H_s^2 d<M>_s], the isometry from L^2(d<M>) into square-integrable martingales that defines the stochastic integral against a square-integrable martingale.

name: stochastic integral with respect to a semimartingale
description: For a locally bounded predictable H and semimartingale X, the process (H.X)_t=int_0^t H_s dX_s defined by linearity over the martingale and finite-variation parts, itself a semimartingale and a local martingale when X is.

name: Kunita-Watanabe inequality
description: For semimartingales M,N and measurable processes H,K, int |H_s||K_s||d[M,N]_s| <= (int H_s^2 d[M])^{1/2}(int K_s^2 d[N])^{1/2}, a pathwise Cauchy-Schwarz bound for covariation integrals.

name: integration by parts for semimartingales
description: Expresses the product as X_t Y_t=X_0 Y_0+int X_{s-}dY_s+int Y_{s-}dX_s+[X,Y]_t, the stochastic product rule whose extra covariation term distinguishes it from classical integration by parts.

name: Ito formula for jump semimartingales
description: For a general semimartingale X and f in C^2, f(X_t)=f(X_0)+int f'(X_{s-})dX_s+1/2 int f''(X_{s-})d[X]^c_s+sum_{s<=t}[f(X_s)-f(X_{s-})-f'(X_{s-})Delta X_s], adding a jump correction to the continuous Ito formula.

name: increasing process and its Stieltjes measure
description: A right-continuous nondecreasing adapted process A that induces, pathwise, a random Lebesgue-Stieltjes measure dA_s on [0,infinity), against which pathwise integrals int H_s dA_s are defined.

name: random measure
description: A measurable map from a probability space into the space of (sigma-finite) measures on a state space, so that M(A) is a random variable for each measurable A; the framework subsuming point processes and Poisson random measures.

name: point process (counting random measure)
description: A random measure N taking nonnegative-integer values on bounded sets, N=sum delta_{T_i}, representing a random configuration of points; its distribution is determined by the joint laws of the counts N(A).

name: intensity (mean) measure of a random measure
description: The deterministic measure nu(A)=E[N(A)] giving the expected number of points (or expected mass) in each set A, the first-moment measure of a point process or random measure.

name: Laplace functional of a Poisson random measure
description: Characterizes a Poisson random measure N with intensity nu via E[exp(-int f dN)]=exp(-int(1-e^{-f})dnu) for nonnegative f, uniquely identifying its law and linearizing computations over independent regions.

name: integral with respect to a Poisson random measure
description: The random variable int f dN=sum f(T_i) summing a function over the atoms of a Poisson random measure N, defined for f with int(|f|^1)dnu<infinity and finite when int|f|dnu<infinity.

name: compensated Poisson integral
description: The centered integral int f d(N-nu)=int f dN-int f dnu against the compensated measure N~=N-nu, a mean-zero (square-integrable when int f^2 dnu<infinity) martingale that is the jump-integral building block of Levy processes.

name: Campbell's theorem
description: For a Poisson random measure with intensity nu, E[int f dN]=int f dnu and Var(int f dN)=int f^2 dnu (when finite), giving the mean and variance of additive functionals of the point configuration.

name: mapping (marking) theorem for Poisson random measures
description: The image of a Poisson random measure of intensity nu under a measurable map T is again a Poisson random measure, with intensity the pushforward T_*nu; independent marking similarly yields a Poisson measure on the enlarged space.

name: subordinator
description: A one-dimensional Levy process with nondecreasing (almost surely increasing) paths, equivalently with Levy triplet having no Gaussian part, nonnegative drift, and Levy measure supported on (0,infinity); used as a random time change.

name: subordination (time change by a subordinator)
description: Constructs a new process Y_t=X_{S_t} by running a Markov or Levy process X along the random clock of an independent subordinator S, producing e.g. the Cauchy process from Brownian motion via a 1/2-stable subordinator.

name: characteristic exponent of a Levy process
description: The function psi with E[e^{iuX_t}]=e^{-t psi(u)}, given by the Levy-Khintchine form psi(u)=-ibu+1/2 sigma^2 u^2+int(1-e^{iux}+iux 1_{|x|<1})nu(dx), encoding the law of the Levy process in a single function.

name: infinitesimal generator of a Levy process
description: The operator Af(x)=bf'(x)+1/2 sigma^2 f''(x)+int[f(x+y)-f(x)-yf'(x)1_{|y|<1}]nu(dy), a Fourier multiplier with symbol -psi(u) whose drift, diffusion, and integral parts mirror the Levy triplet.

name: transition function (Markov semigroup)
description: A family (P_t)_{t>=0} of Markov kernels satisfying P_0=Id and the Chapman-Kolmogorov identity P_{s+t}=P_s P_t, acting on functions by P_t f(x)=int P_t(x,dy)f(y) as the operator semigroup governing a Markov process.

name: canonical realization of a Markov process
description: The construction of a Markov process on the path space Omega=E^{[0,infinity)} (or the cadlag space) with coordinate maps X_t(omega)=omega(t), shift operators theta_t, and the measure P^mu produced from the transition function via the Ionescu-Tulcea/Kolmogorov extension.

name: multidimensional Brownian motion
description: An R^d-valued process whose d coordinates are independent standard one-dimensional Brownian motions, a continuous Gaussian process with stationary independent increments of covariance tI and generator 1/2 Delta.

name: Brownian bridge
description: The process (B_t-tB_1)_{0<=t<=1}, equivalently Brownian motion conditioned to satisfy B_0=B_1=0, a centered Gaussian process with covariance s^t-st.

name: potential of a measure (Green function)
description: The function Umu(x)=int U(x,dy)mu(dy) obtained by applying the potential (Green) kernel of a transient Markov process to a measure mu, an excessive function representing the expected occupation generated by charge mu.

name: stochastic Fubini theorem
description: Permits interchange of an ordinary integral and a stochastic integral, int(int H(s,a)dX_s)lambda(da)=int(int H(s,a)lambda(da))dX_s, under joint measurability and an integrability condition on H.

name: Ito-Tanaka formula (convex functions)
description: For a convex (or difference-of-convex) f, f(X_t)=f(X_0)+int f'_-(X_s)dX_s+1/2 int L_t^a(X)f''(da), extending Ito's formula to non-C^2 functions by integrating local time against the second-derivative measure f''.
